hypotheses.reasoning: At 11:51:40 order-service v2.25.0 rolled out with config revision 692 (#2288). At 11:52:05 order-service loaded that revision, which changed PAYMENT_SVC_URL to http://payment-svc.internal:9090 (#2374). The last successful charge was at 11:52:17. After that, every call to payment-svc on 10.25.9.90:9090 failed with ECONNREFUSED within about 1ms (#2480, #2530, #2631, #2729). payment-svc itself stayed healthy and logged no errors. It simply stopped receiving /charge requests, so the new endpoint is wrong, most likely the wrong port. Because order-service could not charge, it returned 503s, and the gateway's POST /checkout success rate fell to 0%. The report-cron pandas failure and the order-consumer deploy are unrelated to the checkout path.

This is the same fault read a different way. The wrong PAYMENT_SVC_URL came in through a config-service reload, which is a misconfigured endpoint. It only falls short of being the top answer because the revision shipped together with the v2.25.0 release.
Connection refused could mean payment-svc is down. But payment-svc kept logging normally and nothing in its logs shows it went down, so this is unlikely.

verdict.recommendedAction: Roll back order-service to the previous release and config (revert revision 692), or set PAYMENT_SVC_URL back to payment-svc's correct listening port. Then check that /charge calls succeed and /checkout recovers. Add a startup or readiness check so a bad dependency endpoint fails the rollout instead of reaching production.
